assignment.assignmentRationale: Highest explicit policy priority, then lexical profile ID.

forbiddenActions: Do not select or change the target ref, expected commit, source commit, strategy, adapter identity, permissions, or verified bytes.
Do not resolve conflicts automatically, approve integration, create graph operations, decide downstream outcomes, update package exports, or mutate the DevRelay repository during tests.
Do not use shell-interpolated command strings; spawn Git with bounded argument arrays in isolated temporary repositories only.
Do not modify non-allowlisted files or create commits, tags, pull requests, or merges in the DevRelay checkout.

bootstrapDisposition.authority: The visible execution task may propose only the bounded local Git adapter, plug-in manifest, and isolated conformance tests. Core retains target selection, CAS authorization, result validation, verification, graph, and progression authority.
bootstrapDisposition.reason: ChangeIntegration is being built, so the task host temporarily performs the released WorkExecution executor-port role.

designConstraint.conflictBoundary: Conflicts return RawIntegrationEffectResult terminalState conflict, effectState not-applied, exact paths and native evidence; the target ref remains unchanged and no resolver runs.
designConstraint.evidenceBoundary: Return exact pre-state, operation, native command evidence, and post-state only when observed.
designConstraint.evidencePersistence: A host-owned evidence sink persists exact canonical bytes and returns the only admissible native ArtifactRef.
designConstraint.runtimeAuthorization: The adapter port artifact remains IntegrationAdapterInvocation. A host-only runtime context must supply the exact authorized invocationFingerprint, targetRef, and expectedTargetCommit from the Core TARGET-CAS request; any resealed operation has a different fingerprint and fails before Git.
designConstraint.summary: Implement a provider-neutral port adapter for one local Git repository. It receives the exact IntegrationAdapterInvocation authorized by Core and performs one atomic expected-ref transition. Candidate commits may be prepared in an isolated temporary worktree, but the configured target ref may change only through git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected> or an equivalent atomic primitive.
designConstraint.uncertaintyBoundary: Interruption or an unprovable post-effect state returns interrupted/uncertain evidence; never infer success from process exit alone.

incomingEdges.rationale: The adapter must implement the canonical integration port.
The adapter may run only after exact target authorization.

requiredCorrections: Define one canonical serializable adapter configuration material (repositoryPath, gitExecutable, bounded timeout/policy fields), compute its configurationDigest, and require invocation.adapter to match ID, version, and that exact digest before any Git call.

Require a host-owned persistNativeEvidence(bytes, metadata) callback or equivalent evidence store. Persist canonical command-evidence bytes, validate the returned ArtifactRef digest against those exact bytes, and only then cite it in RawIntegrationEffectResult. Never fabricate an unretrievable ref.
Add a bounded Git timeout and preserve timeout/signal as interrupted evidence; do not hang indefinitely.

Add explicit zero-effect or fail-closed fixtures for configuration substitution, wrong target, changed/resealed operation versus the Core authorization supplied by the host, denied spawn, interrupted process, malformed evidence-store response, and native-evidence byte retrieval/digest verification.

Preserve all three clean strategies, isolated candidate preparation, conflict no-mutation, atomic update-ref expected-old behavior, plug-in conformance, and the rule that only Core may supply target/operation authority.
stopConditions: Stop with clarify if the three approved strategies cannot be implemented behind the existing port without a public contract change.
Stop with block if Git or exact test dependencies are unavailable.
Stop after the bounded handoff; do not begin checkpoint recovery.
Stop with fix if any mismatch can mutate the target, any conflict is auto-resolved, or any test touches the DevRelay checkout.

verification.acceptance: Clean fast-forward, merge-commit, and cherry-pick plus conflict, malformed, denied, interrupted, wrong-target, changed-operation, adapter substitution, and concurrent-ref fixtures prove one authorized atomic effect and no lifecycle authority.

requiredEvidence.description: The adapter performs only one authorized conditional local Git effect and never resolves conflicts or claims lifecycle authority.

excluded: Selecting targets, altering verified bytes, automatically resolving conflicts, approving integration, or authoring graph operations.
included: Apply only the exact verified change under the authorized IntegrationPlan.
Return exact native pre-state, operation, conflict or failure, post-state, and raw evidence.
